records.name: Closed Static Core
records.definition: A core fixed at build time that cannot accept new capabilities without being recompiled.

records.name: Compile-Time Binding

distinctFrom.reason: Compile-time binding fixes the choice in the build, while manual registration lists each component by hand at runtime.

records.definition: Fixing at build time which implementation a call uses or how components are wired together, so neither can vary or be discovered at runtime.

records.name: Hardcoded Endpoints
records.definition: Hardcoding service network addresses instead of discovering them dynamically.

records.name: Manual Registration
records.definition: Requiring each component to be registered by hand instead of being discovered automatically.

records.name: Capability Addition without Core Modification
records.definition: The ability to add new capabilities at runtime without modifying the core.

records.name: Deferred Implementation Choice
records.definition: The ability to postpone choosing a concrete implementation until runtime, so each environment can assemble its own.

records.name: Dynamic Routing
records.definition: The ability to route requests to service instances discovered at runtime.

records.name: Self-Registration
records.definition: The ability for a component to register itself on load without external wiring.

records.name: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism
records.definition: Replacing a branching conditional on type with polymorphic dispatch through a shared interface.

records.name: Runtime Resolution
records.definition: The requirement that a symbol's concrete binding be resolved, by discovery or from configuration, during execution rather than at compile time.

records.name: Extensibility
records.definition: The degree to which new behavior can be added with minimal change to existing code.

records.name: Startup Cost
records.definition: The degree to which scanning for components at startup slows the system's initialization.

records.name: Discovery Validation
records.definition: A technique for checking at startup that every discovered component declares the contract it claims.
